mark_breakdown.desc: Isolate the logarithm and convert to exponential form

subparts.solution:
$f$ is $y = \ln(x+2) - 5$
$\therefore f^{-1}$ is $x = \ln(y+2) - 5$
$\therefore x + 5 = \ln(y+2)$
$\therefore y + 2 = e^{x+5}$
$\therefore y = e^{x+5} - 2$
So, $f^{-1}(x) = e^{x+5} - 2$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The inverse of a logarithmic function $\ln(u)$ is the exponential function $e^u$.
step_by_step: Exponentiate both sides with base $e$: $e^{x+5} = y + 2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Exponentiating before isolating the logarithm, e.g., incorrectly writing $e^x = y + 2 - e^5$.

subparts.stem: On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of $f$ and $f^{-1}$.
subparts.final_answer: $\text{Graph showing } y = f(x) \text{ and } y = f^{-1}(x) \text{ reflected across } y = x$

mark_breakdown.desc: Sketch $y = f^{-1}(x)$ with horizontal asymptote $y = -2$, showing reflection across $y = x$

subparts.solution:
The graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ is a reflection of the graph of $y = f(x)$ in the line $y = x$.
$y = f(x)$ has vertical asymptote $x = -2$.
$y = f^{-1}(x)$ has horizontal asymptote $y = -2$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Inverse functions reflect across the diagonal line $y = x$; vertical asymptotes $x = c$ become horizontal asymptotes $y = c$.
step_by_step: Draw $f^{-1}(x) = e^{x+5}-2$ with horizontal asymptote $y = -2$ as its reflection across $y = x$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Drawing the asymptote of the inverse function at $x = -2$ rather than $y = -2$.

subparts.stem: State the domain and range of $f^{-1}$.

mark_breakdown.desc: State the domain of $f^{-1}$ as $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$
State the range of $f^{-1}$ as $\{y \mid y > -2\}$

subparts.solution:
The domain of $f^{-1}$ is $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
The range of $f^{-1}$ is $\{y \mid y > -2\}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The exponential function $e^{x+5} - 2$ is defined for all real numbers and is strictly greater than its horizontal asymptote $-2$.
step_by_step: Since $e^{x+5}$ is defined for any real $x$, the domain of $f^{-1}$ is $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
Since $e^{x+5} > 0$ for all $x$, $e^{x+5} - 2 > -2$, so the range is $\{y \mid y > -2\}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Including $-2$ in the range with $\ge$ rather than strictly $>$.
